hits.text: The death notice → Four corrections it offers our own tree: Anna Catharina is recorded there as Slier , not Schleher; her marriage to James Mountjoy is dated 9 March 1817 at Graaff-Reinet ; Thomas Jacobus lived to 1827 , not 1818; and there is a sibling our tree lacks entirely — Jacoba Catharina Mountjoy (1820–1842) . Johanna Margaritha Pretorius — the woman four documents refused to name She was the hardest person in this archive to find, and the reason is worth as much as the answer. hits.text: The query re-surfaced him; it did not find him. He remains exactly what he was: an unresolved second William, indexed twice over to Graaff-Reinet and Dordrecht , eight years after the Burgersdorp baptism . On Henry Jaonas there is an argument, and it comes entirely out of figures this archive already held. John Augustus Barry II was born 13 March 1847 and baptised four weeks later — a documented date, off a register. James Henry Barry is carried in this archive as born "about 1847" , and that figure is not a register at all: it is an age worked back from his death at Barkly East on 23 June 1939. Two brothers cannot both be born in 1847 , and the approximate date is the one that has to give way.

THE YORKSHIRE MAN IS NOW A LIFE: born at WHITBY in 1796; resident at BILSDALE MIDCABLE when he took a licence on 2 October 1838 to marry MARGARET JACKSON of Beadlam at Helmsley; and in the 1851 census a SHIP OWNER at SHIP YARDS, RUSWARP, WHITBY, aged 55, married, head of his household — the ONLY John Barry of that age in the whole Yorkshire census. John Barry deaths are then registered in the WHITBY district in 1858 and in 1860. He outlived the Cape man, who died at de Bruins Poort in 1853, by at least five years. THEY ARE TWO MEN. What this archive still does not have is the Cape one: no birth, no arrival, no burial. And a caution worth keeping — a Whitby SHIP OWNER is exactly the kind of man whose son could be born AT SEA, which is what John Augustus Barry's death notice says of 1819. That coincidence is not evidence, and the censuses say it is not the same man.

john-gerson-eliezar-kolbe.v: “Jan” · JOHN GERSON ELIEZER KOLBE, in his obituary · Commandant Kolbe
john-gerson-eliezar-kolbe.r: THE SETTLER'S ELDEST CHILD, AND UNTIL TODAY A LINE IN A TABLE. His obituary — Grahamstown Journal, 15 April 1868, headed “DEATH OF COMMANDANT KOLBE” — gives the whole man. Born 7 JULY 1822; married 3 APRIL 1843 to ANNA JACOBA VAN DER MERWE; DIED 3 APRIL 1868, ON HIS WEDDING ANNIVERSARY, at the farm LEEUWBERG, of TYPHUS OR TYPHOID CAUGHT ON COMMANDO — “thus adding another to the long list of victims of our miserable war”. He had settled on KAALSPRUIT about 1850 and lies there — AND HE CONFIRMS THE FARM HIMSELF. A lost-property advertisement he placed in the Friend on 9 MARCH 1864 is signed “J.G.E. KOLBE, Kafferberg, Kaalspruit” (the address as the paper printed it). The Friend’s own obituary transcription reads “[Randspruit]”, bracketed by the transcriber as doubtful; the man’s own address settles it. THAT ADVERTISEMENT ALSO PUTS THE TWO BROTHERS IN ONE DOCUMENT: it concerns “a promissory note, date 9th March 1864, drawn by GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE in favor of J.G.E. KOLBE, payable 4 months after date for £154 Stg” — lost on the Market Square at Bloemfontein. HE LEFT A WIDOW AND TWELVE CHILDREN — “OF THE EIGHT SONS AND FOUR DAUGHTERS HE HAS LEFT BEHIND HIM”, which is the Friend of the Free State’s own wording and a count the Grahamstown reprint drops. Only one daughter was married and the youngest child was an infant; TWO SONS HAD BEEN SERVING WITH HIM IN THE FIELD and “proved themselves amongst the bravest of our burghers”. NONE OF THE TWELVE IS NAMED AND NONE IS IN THIS ARCHIVE. 20 SEPTEMBER 2026 — A COLLABORATIVE TREE NAMES THEM, AND IT IS NOT THIS FAMILY’S OWN. A Geni profile for FREDERIK FORTUNATUS KOLBE, born 22 October 1857 at Bloemfontein and dead there 18 December 1930, gives him as SON OF COMMANDANT.GEN. JOHN GHERSON ELIEZER KOLBE AND ANNA JACOBA, and lists as his siblings CATHARINA WILHELMINA MAGDALENA PIENAAR ANDERSON, GEORGE AUGUSTUS, GENERAL WILLEM JOHANNES, JAN HENDRIK and PETRUS JACOBUS “and 6 others” — which is twelve. THIS IS FROM A USER TREE, NOT FROM A DOCUMENT, and none of the twelve is adopted here on it — it is a lead and not a witness. But TWO OF ITS CLAIMS MATCH DOCUMENTS THIS ARCHIVE REACHED INDEPENDENTLY: his wife MARIA PETRONELLA ELIZABETH ANTOINETTE and daughter ROSA MAGDALENE against the 1890 Bloemfontein baptism already held, and his daughter MARIA MARGARETHA DOWNING ROUSSEAU against TAB MHG 5450/68, an orphan index entry here that now has a father. VAB MHG M777 IS STILL THE DOCUMENT THAT WOULD PROVE THEM, and it is a better thing to order now that there is something to check it against. He was COMMANDANT OF THE DISTRICT, A JUSTICE OF THE PEACE, A DIRECTOR OF THE BLOEMFONTEIN BANK and a DEACON of the Dutch Reformed Church, and he had spoken in the VOLKSRAAD in May 1867. He had refused public life for twelve years after THE ABANDONMENT, having protested the British withdrawal and applied to SIR GEORGE CLERK for compensation for his land so that he might leave with the troops; failing that, “he, like many more, had to cast his lot with the Free State”. AND ON HIS DEATHBED, in full possession of his senses, he told the doctor and the others present THAT THIS STATE HAD TAKEN TOO MUCH LAND FROM THE BASUTOS, that he had always thought so and had said so in the Raad, and begged them to rescind the resolution and treat with the Governor for an equitable boundary. 20 SEPTEMBER 2026 — A HISTORIAN’S DRAFT NAMES HIM TOO, AND NAMES THE WAR. The DSAB entry on his father says the eldest son “J.G.E. KOLBE (1822–68), was later op LEEUBERG naby Bloemfontein woonagtig en het gedurende die TWEEDE SOTHO-VRYSTAATOORLOG roem verwerf as KOMMANDANT”. BOTH YEARS MATCH THIS ARCHIVE TO THE YEAR — born 7 July 1822, dead 3 April 1868 — and both were got from an obituary and an auction advertisement that the entry does not cite. It is the strongest of the nine places where that entry and this archive agree from different documents. AND IT NAMES WHAT KILLED HIM: the obituary said only “our miserable war”; the war was the SECOND SOTHO–FREE STATE WAR. AND HE MAY BE IN THE 1830 LETTER, AGED EIGHT. Read from the file rather than from a mail preview, MSB 751 encloses “a Jacket & waistcoat FOR JOHN & a further Jacket also for him, tell him HIS OLD FATHER has sent it him, & TO MAKE HASTE TO FILL THEM OUT”. CLOTHES FOR A GROWING CHILD, sent from Soho to the Cape in August 1830, when this man was eight years old and the eldest son of the house. IF IT IS HIM IT IS THE EARLIEST DOCUMENT IN THIS ARCHIVE THAT MENTIONS HIM. “His old father” is the difficulty and is not glossed over — the writer is his GRANDFATHER, and this is an inference, not a reading.

john-henry-kolbe.d: 13 Apr 1832, buried 22 Apr 1832, German Lutheran Church
john-henry-kolbe.r: ONE OF THE EIGHT SONS, AND THE ONE WHO LIVED LONGEST OF THOSE FOUND. Baptised 29 July 1800, father John, mother Mary, batch I02559-1. TNA RG 4/4631 folio 100: died 13 April 1832, buried 22 April, AGED 32 — twelve years before the obituary that counted him among the seven already gone. AND HE SPEAKS. Old Bailey, session of 13 January 1819, trial t18190113-149 — Richard Kerr indicted for stealing “one coat, value 6l., the property of JOHN HENRY KOLBE”. His own deposition: “MY FATHER IS A TAILOR, AND LIVES IN CHURCH-STREET, SOHO. On the 9th of January, about eleven o’clock at night, I stopped at the Star and Crown public-house, Westminster, and left my coat over my horse’s head — I had a chaise standing at the door; I saw the prisoner go out, and suspected him — I went out, and missed my coat.” NOT GUILTY. HE WAS EIGHTEEN, and his brother George Augustus sailed for Algoa Bay the following year. It is the only voice this archive has from the Soho house, and it corroborates the rate books’ address from a source that had no interest in it. AND THE LONDON GAZETTE SAYS WHAT BECAME OF HIM. 12 MAY 1824, issue 18027 page 796: the partnership of “JOHN GOTLOB KOLBE AND JOHN HENRY KOLBE, OF CHURCH-STREET, SOHO, IN THE COUNTY OF MIDDLESEX, TAILORS” dissolved — father and son, in business together, at the address he gave the court five years earlier. Then 9 OCTOBER and 16 NOVEMBER 1824, issues 18069 page 1668 and 18080 page 1900, in the INSOLVENT DEBTORS lists, petitions to be heard at Portugal-Street, Lincoln’s-Inn Fields on 5 November: “KOLBE, JOHN HENRY (SUED AS HENRY KOLBE), FORMERLY OF NO. 22, NORFOLK-STREET, MIDDLESEX-HOSPITAL, AND LATE OF NO. 4, MANSFIELD-PLACE”. HE WAS TWENTY-FOUR, OUT OF THE FAMILY BUSINESS AND OUT OF SOHO IN THE SAME YEAR HIS STEPMOTHER DIED, and he was dead at thirty-two. 20 SEPTEMBER 2026 — AND HIS FATHER WRITES ABOUT HIS DYING. MSB 751, the letter of 23 August 1830 to his brother at the Cape: “HENRY had wrote to you himself & left his letter at the Mission house to be forwarded to you… he keeps up pretty well at present, but what effect the winter may have upon him if it should set in very cold, as it did last winter, is perhaps not doubtful, since it must prevent him from taking exercise by walking, & which is a great means of keeping down THE DROPSY, OF WHICH HE BEARS STILL THE SYMPTOMS… I trust also that you will join your prayers, that he may vouchsafe to prepare him to a fit state of meeting his God… HE APPEARS AT PRESENT TO BE RESIGNED TO THE CATASTROPHE.” HE HAD TWENTY MONTHS LEFT. And the same letter’s closing — “kind love from your SISTERS & BROTHER” — makes him THE LAST OF THE EIGHT SONS ALIVE BESIDES GEORGE AUGUSTUS, so that the obituary’s “last remaining of eight sons” became true on 13 April 1832, twelve years before it was printed. AND HE MARRIED THREE MONTHS AFTER THE TRIAL: Westminster Marriages — JOHN HENRY KOLBE AND MATILDA FORD, 26 APRIL 1819, ST MARGARET WESTMINSTER, both of that parish. He was eighteen. A MARY ANN MARIA FORD KOLBE MARRIED AT WHITECHAPEL IN THE FIRST QUARTER OF 1847 — GRO index volume AZ, 840, page 16 — and “Ford” carried as a forename is how families carried a mother’s maiden name. SHE IS VERY PROBABLY HIS DAUGHTER. AND THE PRESS GIVES HIS TRADE, WHICH THE GAZETTE DID NOT. Law Chronicle, Commercial and Bankruptcy Register, 13 January 1825: “KOLBE John Henry, of Norfolk-street, Middlesex-hospital, LAST OF MANSFIELD-ST., KENTISH TOWN, TAILOR, DRAPER” — so he set up on his own account in his father’s trade, and the Gazette’s “Mansfield-Place” is Mansfield Street, Kentish Town. THE MAY 1824 DISSOLUTION WAS REPORTED IN AT LEAST SIX LONDON PAPERS, all of them putting HIS name first: “J. H. Kolbe and J. G. Kolbe, Church-street, Soho, tailors”. AND THE 1830 LETTER SHOWS HIM DOING AN ORDINARY THING. Packing a year of newspapers for the Cape, his father notes one number missing — “the one of the 4th of Decr last, which cannot be found, supposing that HENRY, WHO HAS THEM EVERY WEEK, AFTER I HAVE DONE WITH THEM, — has lost”. The father read the paper first and the son had it after. IT IS THE ONLY DESCRIPTION THIS ARCHIVE HAS OF WHAT ANYBODY IN THAT HOUSE DID WITH AN ORDINARY EVENING, and he had four months to live when it was written.

margaret-downing.d: 2_ Nov 1867, Burgersdorp — the day illegible on the stone
margaret-downing.r: THE ANSWER WAS ON A PHOTOGRAPH THIS ARCHIVE HAS HAD ALL ALONG. The Burgersdorp monument is on the Kolbe page, and the caption quoted it as far as “ALSO HIS RELICT MARGARET DOWNING…” AND STOPPED THERE. The stone goes on: “BORN IN LONDON 23 FEBRUARY 1803 AND DIED AT BURGHERSDORP 2_ NOVEMBER 1867.” HER BIRTH IS NOW A DATE — 23 February 1803, where this archive had “c. 1804” — AND THE DEATH IS SETTLED AT 1867. Her son’s obituary of 15 April 1868 said she had died “about three months since”, which would have been January 1868; it was nearly five months, and a journalist rounding is a journalist rounding. THE DAY IS A 2 AND A DIGIT THAT WILL NOT RESOLVE at any magnification, and is not guessed. The Cape estate ran on: MOOC 13/1/253 no. 2, “DOWNING, MARGARET, WIDOW OF KOLBE, GEORGE AUGUSTUS. LIQUIDATION AND DISTRIBUTION ACCOUNT”, 1869 — and she had made a WILL OF HER OWN in 1854, MOOC 7/1/295 no. 70, ten years after she was widowed. Married at fifteen in Shoreditch, signing with a mark. Died owning a house and a farm. 20 SEPTEMBER 2026 — HER MOTHER IS STILL NOBODY, AND THAT IS NOW A TESTED POSITION RATHER THAN A GAP. A user tree gave her as MARY KING POOLEY (1768–1834); this archive’s own copy of the tree gives MARY P KING. FindMyPast holds exactly ONE Downing–Pooley marriage before civil registration — JOHN DOWNING and MARY POOLEY at WELCOMBE, DEVON, 10 MAY 1802, nine months and thirteen days before Margaret’s birth — AND THAT COUPLE STAYED IN DEVON, baptising a child at Welcombe in 1803 and more in 1806, 1809 and 1810, where Margaret was born in LONDON. RULED OUT. And the last Downing record in that parish is A MARY DOWNING BURIED THERE IN 1834, which is the year both trees give her mother’s death — SO “POOLEY” IS VERY PROBABLY A PREVIOUS RESEARCHER’S RECONSTRUCTION out of one Devon marriage and one Devon burial, and not a record at all. FROM A USER TREE, NOT ADOPTED. Her own 1867 death notice asks for her parents and answers “Both dead”, naming neither. AND THERE IS A CERTIFICATE, IN A MUSEUM. The DSAB draft on her husband lists among its sources “ALBANY MUSEUM, GRAHAMSTAD: FOTOKOPIE VAN DIE HUWELIKSSERTIFIKAAT VAN G.A. KOLBE (1819)”. THIS ARCHIVE HOLDS THE ALLEGATION AND NOT THE MARRIAGE — the sworn statement made to get the licence, which is where the false age was sworn, and not the register entry that followed it. A photocopy of the certificate has been sitting in Grahamstown since before 1992. The same entry gives her dates as “(1803–1867)”, WHICH IS WHAT THE BURGERSDORP STONE SAYS, from a source that had not read the stone this way.

His grandfather was George Augustus Kolbe — who married at sixteen on a sworn lie in Shoreditch, sailed on the Nautilus in 1819 as an 1820 Settler , preached across the Orange River, and named a Karoo farm after the Württemberg his own father had left. His grandmother was Margaret Downing of London. Both of them lie under a cut-stone monument at Burgersdorp — names, London birthplaces, farm and dates carved into it — about forty miles from where that notice was written. The family forgot them inside seventy years, with the headstone still standing. And it had happened before, on the other side of the house.

hits.title: The cousin marriage
hits.text: George was Kathleen's son. Anna was Hendrik's granddaughter. They were first cousins once removed , and their common ancestors are John Augustus Barry I and Margaretha Wilhelmina Elizabeth Mary Kolbe . What follows from it Catherine Mary Sophia Booyzen descends from John Augustus Barry I and Margaretha Kolbe twice — once through her father, once through her mother. This is pedigree collapse : she has fewer distinct ancestors than the arithmetic of generations predicts.

hits.text: Checked one by one against the register here, nearly all of them were already held: Harriet Louisa Barry , dead at Manor Owen on 7 September 1912; Henry James Kolbe Barry , whose 23 June 1939 is already on his record; John Gerson Eliazer Barry ; James Jonathan Mountjoy , dead at Barkly East on 22 December 1937; and Margaretha Wilhelmina Elizabeth Mary Kolbe , dead at Manorowen on 2 August 1912. That is worth saying rather than quietly not saying. A sweep that returns almost nothing new is a measurement of how thoroughly the ground was already worked, and this ground was worked properly. The work-list row assumed otherwise. One discrepancy, recorded and not adopted.

hits.title: The cousin marriage
hits.text: The Schoemans sit alongside the Barrys in the same way. P. Schoeman witnessed the 1879 Booysen–Barry marriage ; Anna Johanna Maria Schoemann married Hendrik Nicholaas Barry in 1877; and the 1901 Pretorius–Barry wedding was held at the home of D. Schoeman . Why that matters → The names give it away Anna's mother was christened Margarietha Wilhelmina Elizabeth Barry — the same four names, in the same order, as her own grandmother Margaretha Wilhelmina Elizabeth Mary Kolbe . And Anna herself was "named after Anna Johanna Maria Schoemann" , her father's mother, a fact the tree records explicitly rather than leaving to be inferred.

hits.title: The rebels
hits.text: Jerpoint is new, and it is Irish — which is where the Barrys are supposed to have come from, and where this archive has never been able to place them. Open questions → A coincidence worth chasing: Commandant D. Schoeman On 8 July 1901 — with martial law in force and the war still running — Margarietha Wilhelmina Elizabeth Barry married Petrus Jacobus Pretorius . The tree records the venue with unusual precision: "At the home of D Schoeman , 'Caerlaverock' , Barkly East district, Cape Colony." In March 1900 , about 400 Cape Rebels under Commandant D. Schoeman held Labuschagne's Nek, north of Dordrecht — the next district over. The bride's mother was Anna Johanna Maria Schoemann .

The 1903 registration of her father's death says ELEVEN children; his own death notice names eight and her mother's names nine. SHE IS IN THE BURGERSDORP REGISTER AND NOT IN ANY NAME SEARCH, BECAUSE THE INDEX GIVES HER NO SURNAME: two separate index passes of the same page read “MARGRITH LOUISA MARIA” and “MARGRETH LOUISA MARY”, and the Name column stops there. It is the blank Name column again, the same failure that hid her sister Catherine Mary Sophia of 1855. Found by asking the index for a RELATIONSHIP — father John Barry, mother a Kolbe — and letting it return whatever the child was called. Her parents are entered as “Margrith Willemina Kolbe + John Barry”. SHE IS ALMOST CERTAINLY THE “MARGARET MARY” NAMED ON HER PARENTS' DEATH NOTICES AND NEVER PLACED: it is her mother's name, and there is no other candidate in the sibling group. ark:/61903/1:1:6VYG-SS94 and 1:1:6F4L-76PK.

hits.text: So of the three figures the archive had, the marriage register is the outlier : it gives his age as 22 in December 1879, when he was 28 . His 1905 death registration says 55 , which is right within a year. The 1879 entry is wrong by six years. And he was named for his godfather The witnesses are Willem Hermanus Pieterzen , Maria Catharina Magdalena Potgieter and Xaverius Hermanus Pieterzen . (The archive scan corrects this archive's earlier reading of the surname as Pietersen — see below; the first given name, earlier read as Iwerus , is still not certain.) KOLBE) — 26 OKT. 1886 – 1 OKT. 1953 — Wat hy doen is wel gedaan.” And underneath, six household names: MARTZI · P.S. · JUDIE · PIETMAN · CHARL EN SUZAN. THE BIRTH IS NOW A DATE — 26 October 1886, where this archive had only the year — and THE SIX CHILDREN ARE NEW. This is the THIRD stone in this archive to list children by what they were called rather than what they were registered as: the Booyzens at Silverton, the Kolbes at Wakkerstroom, and now this. BORN AT WAKKERSTROOM AND DEAD AT WAKKERSTROOM, sixty-seven years apart, in a town her grandfather had never seen. Her 1953 estate file is the document that names the whole household: FATHER George Augustus Kolbe, MOTHER Martha Sophia Klopper, HUSBAND Charl Daniel van der Merwe. Her birthplace is entered as “Wakkerstroomn, Transvaal, Blanke Unie-burger” — the clerk's spelling, and the Union's category.

hits.title: The Booyzen Archive
hits.text: There is no photograph of their farm, and this archive does not invent one. This archive was built for David Defranceski , born in Johannesburg, living in Brisbane. It runs backwards from his grandmother Catherine Mary Sophia Booyzen (1929–2013) — who married Nuno Fernando Lerena at St Joseph's, Mayfair, in 1949 — into the north-eastern Cape: to Barkly East and Dordrecht , to Cradock and Graaff-Reinet , and out again to Württemberg , to Soho , and to a County Cork that may or may not be real. It is a public archive with one rule: the living are left out — omitted, not hidden. And a second rule, which is harder: every claim says how well it is known.

petrus-jacobus-booyzen.r: HIS STONE IS READ AND IT CONFIRMS BOTH DATES EXACTLY: “HIER RUS — MY GELIEFDE SEUN — PIETER J. BOOYZEN — GEB. 29 DES. 1904 — OORL. 7 JUNIE 1937 — NA DIE KRUIS DIE KROON.” Dead at thirty-two. AND ONE WORD OF IT DOES REAL WORK: “MY geliefde seun”, not “ONS”. A stone cut by ONE surviving parent — and his mother Isabella Frederika had been dead seven years when he died, so the parent is his father, GERT JACOBUS, who then lay down beside them both fourteen years later. Three of one household in one cemetery, and the grammar of the inscriptions gives the order they went in. Baptised in the Dutch Reformed register with a Z, son of Gert Jacobus Booyzen and Isabella Frederika Coetzee — the second marriage's line, at Middelburg, spelled Booyzen a year before the Indwe sheet.

hits.title: Disputed
hits.text: FamilySearch carries a Dutch Reformed marriage of PETRUS JACOBUS BOOŸZEN and ANNA MARIA VAN DER MERWE dated 9 MARCH 1825, at Cape Town, indexed three separate times. Resolved RESOLVED, 13 September 2026. A Dutch Reformed baptism names DAVID SCHALK BOOIJZEN, born 12 DECEMBER 1806, as the son of Pieter Jacobus Booijzen and ANNA MARIA VAN DER MERWE — and he is first of the eight on the 1876 Sterfkennis. They were married BY 1806, so the 1805 marriage at Graaff-Reinet stands and the 1825 Cape Town record is a different couple of the same two very common names. It also rewrites the wall on the ancestor chart, which said “only a family tree puts her here”. It no longer does.

hits.text: So the van Niekerks are now documented. Maria Sophia van Niekerk , who married Hercules Johannes Mountjoy at Dordrecht on 8 October 1888, was a daughter of Jan Dirk Abram Frans van Niekerk and Carolina Deybella Margrietta Alletta Botha , who was herself born in the district of Cradock and whose parents were Philip Rudolph Botha and a mother of the same long name. Her ten brothers and sisters were Carolina Deybella Margrietta Alletta, Cornelius, Maria Francina Cecilia (widow of Gert Olivier), Jan Dirk Abram Frans, Hercules Johannes , Christiaan Jacobus, Cornelia Elizabeth Gertruida (married James Ross), Benjamin Jacobus, Pieter Jacobus and Philip Rudolph.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: Catherine Mary Sophia is her own name, and her mother's before her — Kathleen Barry , born 1859. Margaret Wilhelmina Elizabeth is the Barry name that runs down the other side of this family too. William Herman is Willem Hermanus , her father. Richard Peter is her uncle, Richard Peter Barry . Henry James is her brother. Five of eleven Daschner children carry Booyzen and Barry names. The surname leaves the family in one generation. The names do not. This is the same evidence the archive uses on the name and in the cousin marriage : in this family, forenames are inherited property, and they travel through daughters as reliably as surnames travel through sons.

richard-peter-booyzen.d: 25 Oct 1918, Turffontein — buried 27 Oct, Brixton, D.R., grave 1119
richard-peter-booyzen.r: TWENTY-FOUR, MARRIED, a SAWYER of 18 Anderson Street, Turffontein — dead of INFLUENZA AND PNEUMONIA after eleven days on 25 October 1918, the centre of Black October, and buried at Brixton on the 27th. Not in this archive before today. Added as a ninth child of Willem Hermanus and Kathleen Barry on three grounds and no document: RICHARD PETER is her own brother's name; a birth about 1894 falls exactly in the gap between her daughter of 1891 and her son of 1901; and his registration gives his birthplace as the CAPE OF GOOD HOPE, which is the migration every one of her children made. A Transvaal death registration names no parents, so this stays INFERRED. And he was NOT A SOLDIER — which kills the best explanation this archive had for his mother's military pension.

richard-pieter-kolbe-barry.r: AND THE NAME IS IN A GOVERNMENT FILE, TWICE OVER, IN ONE LINE. SAB, VWR volume 2, reference B645/8/38, 1937: “AANSOEK DEUR PLAASEIENAAR BARKLY-OOS. RPK BARRY. BYWONER RPK BARRY (SEUN).” An application by a farm owner at Barkly East — R.P.K. BARRY — and the bywoner on the place is R.P.K. BARRY, HIS SON. TWO MEN OF THESE INITIALS AT BARKLY EAST IN 1937, one holding the land and one working it as a tenant, and the state file is between them. This archive cannot say which of the two is the man born in 1899 and does not guess. A BYWONER is not a labourer and not an owner; it is the word South Africa used in the 1930s for a white tenant farming another man's ground, and VWR is the Department of Social Welfare. THE FILE HAS NOT BEEN READ. CARRIES BOTH NAMES AT ONCE — Richard Pieter, for the Barry of Manorowen, and Kolbe, for the 1820 Settler family his great-grandmother married out of. Married Maria Magdalena Siebert. FROM THE INDEX; no image read.

stephanus-francois-booyzen.r: THE STONE IS NOW READ, and it is the fullest document this archive has for him. SILVERTON, PRETORIA, a double stone under one base reading BOOYZEN: “'n SIMBOOL VAN LIEFDE — AAN MY DIERBARE EGGENOOT EN ONS VADER — STEFANUS FRANCOIS — ✳ 29-9-1874, † 14-5-1940 — Sy plek is leeg, sy stem is stil, ons swyg o'Heer, dit is Gods wil. Ges. 75:1”. HIS BIRTH IS NOW EXACT: 29 SEPTEMBER 1874, where this archive had only “c. October 1874”. And a pillar between the two halves lists TWELVE CHILDREN by their household names — OUBOET · OUSIE · BESSIE · BETIE · HENNA · EVERT · ✝BABA · FANIE · WILLIE · PIETIE · JOHAN · HENNIE — one of them marked dead with a cross. This archive had almost none of them. They are nicknames, not names on a register, and nothing is claimed from them beyond the count. HIS GRAVE IS FOUND AND PHOTOGRAPHED: “BOOYZEN STEFANUS FRANCOIS 1874-1940”, SILVERTON MAIN CEMETERY, PRETORIA — a joint stone with his wife, “BOOYZEN BEATRIX MAGDALENA CATHARINA NEE BOSHOFF 1889-1977”. Both dates match this archive exactly, and hers is the first death year it has had for her. He died at East Lynne, Pretoria, and lies at Silverton. IMAGE LOCATED, NOT YET READ. PRISONER OF WAR. A printed transport list in the Pretoria government archives, image group 008019246, carries THREE CONSECUTIVE BOOYZENS shipped on the CITY OF CAMBRIDGE on 3 JUNE 1901, all entered from PRETORIA: 18463 STEPHANUS FRANCOIS, 28 · 18464 PETRUS JACOBUS, 29 · 18465 DAVID SCHALK, 54. Consecutive numbers on one transport means taken together. Age 28 against this archive's c. October 1874, which would have made him 26. THE FULLER REGISTER WAS THEN FOUND, and it is better than the De List in every respect: item 1 of the same film, image 126, gives all three as living at PRETORIA, riding with the PRETORIA COMMANDO, and TAKEN AT TOLOSBERG ON 25 APRIL 1901. Its ages are 26, 27 and 53, which match this archive's own dates where the De List's 28, 29 and 54 did not. AND THEN THE PRISONER NUMBER LED SOMEWHERE ELSE ENTIRELY. The medal-roll database at angloboerwar.com holds an entry for a STEPHANUS FRANCOIS BOOYSEN, BURGER, whose PoW number is 18463 — the same number as the register — and it says he was a ZARP, one of the ZAR's police, based at PRETORIA. Quoting a City Coins auction catalogue of November 2020 that described his ABO medal and the papers with it: in action at TALANA, MODDER SPRUIT, COLENSO, PLATRAND (WAGON HILL) where he was WOUNDED IN THE RIGHT LEG ABOVE THE KNEE, SPION KOP and DALMANUTHA — the ZARPs' famous last stand. His applications were completed by his commanding officer, COMMANDANT J. P. DE LA C. SCHROEDER. He was one of FORTY-TWO Boers taken at Tolosberg in the Waterval Valley on 25 April 1901, with two guns and much stock, and was sent to INDIA. This archive has NOT seen the medal or the application; it is strong secondary evidence tied to the register by the number and not by the name. WHAT IT DOES TO THE DISPUTE: he is numbered 18463 and David Schalk Booysen is 18465, two apart on the same transport on the same day, and this man died at EAST LYNNE, PRETORIA, which is the district all three were taken in. That is a FOURTH point favouring David Schalk as his father, and the first that does not depend on a forename. It is still not a document naming a parent. PARENTAGE DISPUTED — see below. A son of the second marriage, and a MESSELAAR — a mason, like his half-brother Willem Hermanus at Indwe. His 1940 Sterfkennis was fetched because it should have named his mother; his widow wrote only “oorlede” for both parents. Married BEATRIX MAGDALENA CATHARINA BOSHOFF at Mosselbaai on 5 SEPTEMBER 1905, certificate 1318 — he 30 and a JONKMAN, she SIXTEEN with her parents consenting. Eleven children; left immovable property and a will. THE REGISTER GIVES HIS RESIDENCE AS PRETORIA, and eleven weeks later David Schalk Booijzen of Goede Hoop, Pretoria — whose 1900 notice names an unmarried major son called Stephanus François — remarried in that same city. This archive placed him under Petrus Jacobus on his birth year alone. It is marked SERIOUS on the disputed page and it is not decided.

hits.title: Disputed
hits.text: Documented He was not shot by anybody. The death registration → Inferred Three readings survive, and the archive does not choose between them: The generations are miscounted. Tersia Booyzen was counting from herself, not from the current researcher. Her "great great grandfather" may be a man this archive has not identified. "Shot and killed" is not an execution. It may mean killed in action, or shot during a farm clearance — neither of which would appear on the treason lists.

willem-hermanus-booyzen-of-indwe.r: AN EIGHTH CHILD, and one this archive did not have. Confirmed at Indwe on 31 May 1907, aged 21, entered “Booijzen”. A MIJNWERKER of DUGMORE MIJN when he married Susanna Adriana Roodt, 16, at Indwe on 21 September 1908 — the only miner in five generations of read occupations, and the answer to the last line of the family testimony. Two children in nine months by two women of the same surname, both entered “onecht”. His mother stood godmother at the first font, which is how this archive knows whose son he is. AND THEN JOHANNESBURG: a WILLIAM HERMAN BOOYZEN, 47, born Cape Province, married, EX MINER UNDERGROUND, of 62 Langford Street, Booysens, died at Johannesburg Hospital on 29 July 1932 of a perforated duodenal ulcer after about one day, and was buried at BRIXTON on 31 July. The occupation, the province, the age within a year and the cemetery all fit; no parents are named, because a civil registration does not ask. And then the grave register closes it: GRAVE 6889 holds “Boysen, William” and, thirty-six years later, SUSANNA ADRIANA BOOYZEN, buried 29 August 1968 — the woman he married at Indwe in 1908. Husband and wife in one grave.

hits.title: The Name
hits.text: Five spellings of one woman are a fact about handwriting. Two spellings of one surname are supposed to be a fact about history. The difference is that somebody in this family cared about the second one. And the same page gives the other half of the pattern. Her son was baptised Willem Hermanus Pietersen in 1809; the 1851 Graaff-Reinet register writes the surname Pieterzen , twice, in the hand that wrote Booyzen three lines above. The Pietersens changed nothing either. What the name means A patronymic Booysen is Dutch and means "son of Booy" . Booy is itself a short form of Boudewijn — the Dutch form of Baldwin , from Germanic bald ("bold") and win ("friend").

willem-slier.r: HER FATHER, AND HALF OF A NAME THIS ARCHIVE HAS BEEN TRACKING FOR WEEKS. Of Hamburg; married ANNA CATHARINA FORTMAN on 19 NOVEMBER 1780 at the Cape; four children baptised between 1787 and 1797. His grandson, baptised in 1809, is WILLEM Hermanus Pietersen — Willem for this man and Hermanus for the boy's own father — and that is the whole derivation of a name two Booyzens in the direct line would later carry. HALF OF IT IS GERMAN AND NONE OF IT IS BOOYZEN BLOOD.

hits.title: The Name
hits.text: De Villiers, volume 3, entry 876: “ Willem Slier, van Hamburg , gehuwd 19 November 1780 met Anna Catharina Fortman.” It is a German name. Schlier or Schleer, spoken by a Hamburger and written down by Cape clerks who had never seen it on paper — which is exactly how one woman ends up with five surnames in five documents inside one lifetime. Nobody argues that the Sliers changed their name.

william-barry.r: Found twice in one day. He came in on the 1915 death notice of his mother Margaretha Kolbe, estate 1291, which names NINE children where his father's names eight — and then the Burgersdorp doopregister produced his baptism: WILLIAM FREDRIK, born 23 August 1853, christened 23 October, godparents JOHN KOLBE, ANNA VAN DER MERWE and GEORGE KOLBE. Two of the three are his mother's brothers. A SECOND William Frederick Thomas was baptised in 1861 and this archive cannot say whether the first died or a clerk erred — a doubt re-surfaced, and briefly mistaken for a new find, when the index was asked for every Barry child of a Kolbe mother. He is not on his father's notice, not on the Cape Rebel roll, and nowhere else in this archive. His father's 1903 registration said ELEVEN children; with William there are nine named and two still missing.

williem-johannes-kolbe-of-panfontein.r: TAKEN PRISONER IN 1901, AGED 54, AT PANFONTEIN IN THE BLOEMFONTEIN DISTRICT, and recorded as a Free Stater. TNA WO 108/368 folio 603. Sent to Natal. **AND ON 21 SEPTEMBER 2026 THE LINE IN THE PRISONER LIST GOT A LIFE.** He is **GENERAL WILLEM JOHANNES KOLBE (1847–1941)**, who led the **BLOEMFONTEIN COMMANDO** and commanded the southern districts of Bloemfontein. **Born 9 July 1847 in the district of PHILIPPOLIS** — the place his grandfather preached at, and where Charles Bell drew a Kolbe in the pulpit in 1834. He was at the **siege of KIMBERLEY, where he was made general**, and afterwards at **PAARDEBERG, DRIEFONTEIN and the BRANDWATERKOM**, and he rode in **DE WET'S INVASION OF THE CAPE COLONY in February 1901** — the year he was captured. **Two horses were shot under him.** The French general DE VILLEBOIS-MAREUIL spoke of his leadership with praise; he was liked in his commando and is said to have treated the burghers kindly. **THE SOURCE IS PRINTED, NOT A TREE** — but read at one remove, and that is said plainly. The career above is in *Afrikanergeskiedenis* (Petronel Fourie) and on the Afrikaans Wikipedia. **The pedigree below is on the Wikipedia article only**, which cites **P. J. Nienaber, *Afrikaanse Biografiese Woordeboek* (Voortrekkerpers, 1947), p. 139** and the Fourie piece without saying which carries what; the Fourie piece was read here in full and has no genealogy in it at all, **so Nienaber is the source by elimination and his page has not been seen**. **AND IT NAMES HIS HOUSE.** Father **J. G. E. KOLBE**, mother **ANNA JACOBA VAN DER MERWE**, grandfather **GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE, “a German missionary”**, grandmother **MARGARET DOWNING**, the grandfather at **KNAPDAAR, BURGERSDORP**, the home farm **ONDER-LEEUWBERG in the Bloemfontein district**, and the father **a commandant in the Basuto war of 1865**. Every one of those is held here already and independently, including the two women's names and the farm the Commandant died on. **THE 1847 IN THE PRISONER LIST AND THE 1847 IN THE DICTIONARY ARE THE SAME YEAR, and Panfontein and Onder-Leeuwberg are the same district.** **WHAT IS STILL NOT PROVED**: that the man in the prisoner list is the man in the dictionary. Two documents agreeing on a name, a year and a district is strong and is not a register. **VAB MHG M777**, the widow's 1896 estate, would name all twelve children — and so, in his own words, might *Herinneringe van genl. W J Kolbe* at the Free State Archives.
